A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. Their full text, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite reformatting and added material.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on six multi-agent systems, including attack, defense, error-rate, and case-study results across four tasks.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds GPT-4o evaluations and revised single-agent comparisons.

M1.justification: AutoTransform, AutoInject, Challenger, and Inspector retain their procedures and substantive prompts. GPT-4o is an additional experimental backbone, rather than a new method component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate HumanEval code generation, CIAR arithmetic reasoning, CommonMT translation, and FairEval text evaluation. No additional dataset, task, language, or population is introduced.

E2.justification: The same six multi-agent systems, single-agent comparison, and two defenses remain. The single-agent evaluation changes its source and prompting protocol, but no distinct comparison method is introduced.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 and Appendix A.1 extend RQ1/RQ2 to GPT-4o while keeping the attack generators on GPT-3.5. Section 4.3 replaces literature-sourced single-agent scores with evaluation using Appendix B.2 prompts. Table 5 also introduces recovered performance loss as an additional metric.

E4.justification: The error-rate sensitivity analysis in Section 4.4/Figure 5a is revised, with per-system evidence supplied in Table 3. Appendix A.1 checks whether findings persist with GPT-4o. The existing error-type, role, round, and case studies remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or comparable uncertainty estimates. The new tables do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Appendix A adds GPT-4o results, including hierarchical scores of 76.83 with AutoTransform and 78.35 with AutoInject in Table 1. Figures 3b and 5a revise single-agent and error-rate results; Tables 3–5 add detailed or derived entries. Table 4's MAD semantic-error score of 75.70 conflicts with the retained Figure 5b value near 54.

T1.justification: Table 5 newly defines recovered performance loss as (X − A)/(V − A) × 100%, specifying defended, attacked, and vanilla performance. Other mathematical definitions remain unchanged, and neither version contains theoretical proofs.

C1.justification: The core contributions and claims about architectural resilience, task sensitivity, error injection, and defenses remain. The introduction's new 87.9% recovery summary quantifies the existing defense claim without changing its scope.

C2.justification: Appendix A.1 interprets the GPT-4o results as supporting the earlier architecture and task conclusions. The limitations now describe coverage of two model families and remove v1's proposed future investigation of stronger models for generating attacks.

D1.justification: Appendix B.2 adds complete single-agent prompts, and Appendix A.1 specifies the retained GPT-3.5 attack generators. Conversely, v2 drops the dated GPT-3.5 identifiers that v1 inconsistently reported as 0613 in Section 4.1 and 0125 in Limitations. Code and data access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 6.2 adds Agent Smith (Gu et al., 2024) and briefly discusses malicious-behavior propagation. Most other reference changes update publication details for the same works rather than changing research positioning.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section sequence remain largely intact. v2 makes localized corrections and rewrites, reverses the defense presentation order, adds acknowledgments, and reorganizes prompts, limitations, and broader impacts into appendices.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figure 9 and five numerical tables covering both new results and previously plotted analyses. Figure 5a changes its vertical scale, Figure 8 reorders defense bars and legends, and the document adopts different title, heading, running-header, and appendix layouts.

improvement.justification: GPT-4o validation and explicit single-agent prompts strengthen the evidence and reproducibility. Figure 5a also becomes consistent at the shared Pm = Pe = 0.2 condition. These gains are limited by the new Table 4 discrepancy for MAD's semantic-error score and unresolved model-snapshot specificity.
